title: Clip a gradient, then add noise
statement_md:
`l2_norm(v)` is already defined. Add `clip_gradient(g, C)` returning the per-example gradient scaled down to length `C`.

- if the norm of `g` is at most `C`, return it unchanged
- otherwise multiply the whole vector by `C / norm` - direction survives, size is capped
- return a new list of floats and do not mutate `g`
- raise `ValueError` when `C <= 0`

Clipped at `C = 1`, both `[6, 8]` and `[3, 4]` land on the same point: no single example can contribute more than the number the noise is calibrated against.
mutations: return [a[1] * x for x in a[0]]
